title: Lower mean wall temperature with a localized hot region

paragraphs.text: The Modified field is cooler over most of the wall but develops a hotter terminal strip ({{figure:1}}). Whereas Reference shows a gradual sequence of increasing temperature toward the right-hand edge, Modified combines a cooler extended region with an abrupt increase on the final facet. The common color scale and physical facet widths make this contrast spatially explicit: the hotter strip occupies only a small part of the wall, rather than indicating a general increase in temperature. Accordingly, the whole-wall mean decreases from {{value:reference-mean}} to {{value:modified-mean}} ({{table:1}}). The lower temperatures over the larger region outweigh the terminal increase in the area average, so the lower mean is consistent with, rather than contradicted by, the local high-temperature feature.

The spatial standard deviation nevertheless increases from {{value:reference-sd}} for Reference to {{value:modified-sd}} for Modified. This is not a nearly uniform shift to lower temperature: such a shift would leave the spatial spread unchanged. Instead, the terminal facet becomes more separated in temperature from the cooler remainder of the wall, as the sharper color contrast in {{figure:1}} shows. Its small area limits its influence on the mean, but its large departure from that mean still contributes to the increased spread. Read together, the map and the moments identify a lower average exposure accompanied by less uniform exposure and a more pronounced local hot region. Thus, the mean alone would favor Modified while overlooking the local temperature increase. This comparison characterizes the prescribed temperature distributions; it does not identify the heat-transfer process responsible for them.

captions.1: Prescribed wall-temperature fields for (a) Reference and (b) Modified, shown on the same physical domain and temperature scale. Each facet has constant temperature, and its displayed width follows the supplied boundaries. The fields are synthetic; colors are not interpolated between facets.

observation_notes.1: Actually opened section-input/writing/figures/1.png. The image has two horizontally aligned rectangular wall maps with a shared temperature colorbar. Both fields progress toward warmer colors from left to right; Modified remains darker over the broad left and central region but has a bright, narrow terminal strip across the full wall height. The terminal contrast is markedly sharper than in Reference. Unequal facet widths and the same physical domain are visible. These are qualitative visual observations, checked against all rows of sources/wall.csv; no quantitative image measurements were made.
